goldens.comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
goldens.reasoning: C1 describes the same bug: the end time is computed from slotStartTime when it should use slotEndTime.

goldens.comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))
goldens.reasoning: C2 points out the same problem: comparing dayjs objects with === checks references, not values, so it should use .isSame().

candidates: Line 142 computes end from slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime, making start and end identical. This means the working hours boundary check end > workingHour.endTime only validates the slot start, not the slot end — so a slot starting within working hours but extending past them will incorrectly be allowed.
Line 114 uses === to compare two dayjs objects, which is reference equality and will always be false -- zero-length overrides (blocked days) are never detected. Use .isSame() instead.

Line 123 uses strict isAfter for the end boundary but the start boundary (lines 117-120) uses isBefore || isSame; a slot starting exactly at the override end time passes the check and is incorrectly marked available. Add || slotStartTime.isSame(...) to line 123 for consistency.

When a slot falls within a date override window, checkIfIsAvailable returns true at line 134 without checking the busy array, allowing double bookings during date override periods. The fix: remove the early return true at line 134 and let execution fall through to the busy.every() check at line 153.
